serp_competitors.title: How To Switch Broadband Provider - Which?
serp_competitors.observed_structure: Answer-led essentials box, three numbered steps, deal-selection checklist, postcode comparison control and a short FAQ section.
serp_competitors.content_gap_to_improve: Make the exceptions to One Touch Switch clearer and put regulator citations next to downtime, cooling-off and contract-notification claims.
serp_competitors.useful_ux_patterns: In-page contents, at-a-glance steps and postcode comparison placed at the decision point.
serp_competitors.useful_ui_patterns: Numbered process, concise bullets and a visible comparison input.
serp_competitors.interactive_or_functional_elements: Postcode deal comparison form and save-article control.
serp_competitors.trust_signals: Named specialist author, current update date, survey methodology and links to provider assessment criteria.
serp_competitors.citation_patterns: Links to related Which? research and Ofcom-backed switching rules, with the survey sample owned by Which?.

serp_competitors.title: How to switch broadband provider and save money | MSE
serp_competitors.observed_structure: Large guide with jump links, a three-step switch, exit-fee incentive table, speed guidance, compensation, social tariffs, digital landlines and haggling.
serp_competitors.content_gap_to_improve: Keep the central switching path shorter, distinguish regulatory facts from provider-specific examples and avoid letting adjacent savings topics obscure the task.
serp_competitors.useful_ux_patterns: Prominent summary, worked decision checks, provider incentive table and contextual routes into comparison.
serp_competitors.useful_ui_patterns: Jump navigation, labelled steps, comparison tables and expandable supporting detail.
serp_competitors.interactive_or_functional_elements: Broadband postcode comparison journey and expandable information panels.
serp_competitors.trust_signals: Named utilities analyst and editor, very recent update date, regulator figures and transparent commercial comparison links.
serp_competitors.citation_patterns: Direct links to provider incentive terms, Ofcom data and separate specialist explainers for claims needing more detail.

serp_competitors.title: Check how to switch your internet, phone or TV provider - Citizens Advice
serp_competitors.observed_structure: Long consumer checklist covering pre-contract questions, broadband speeds, digital landlines, switching each service, cooling-off rights and complaints.
serp_competitors.content_gap_to_improve: Use the latest dated One Touch Switch terminology and give a faster broadband-only route before broader phone, TV and accessibility cases.
serp_competitors.useful_ux_patterns: Task-based headings, warnings for digital landlines and direct escalation instructions.
serp_competitors.useful_ui_patterns: Short paragraphs, nested checklists and clearly separated service types.
serp_competitors.interactive_or_functional_elements: Links to Ofcom speed and coverage checkers plus consumer helpline and complaint routes.
serp_competitors.trust_signals: Independent advice charity, official regulator links, helpline details and a visible review date.
serp_competitors.citation_patterns: Inline links to Ofcom for speed, digital-landline and minimum-service rights.

sources.claims_supported: One Touch Switch process, old service ending automatically, no post-switch notice charge, maximum one-working-day loss of service, bundle exceptions and 14-day cooling-off period.
Typical 12, 18 or 24-month terms and mandatory end-of-contract notifications 10 to 40 days before the minimum term ends.
2026 automatic compensation scheme membership and amounts for delayed service start, missed appointments and delayed fault repair.
Gaining provider manages the switch, cross-network scope, start-date updates and possible installation work when changing network or adding full fibre.
A provider implementation of One Touch Switch and an example of provider-owned equipment needing return after departure.
Independent corroboration of the usual three-step process, a roughly 10-working-day planning period and checks for exit fees, speed, price rises and contract length.
Independent guidance on provider notifications, bundle services, landline number transfer, final bills and complaint escalation.

required_sections: Contract and early termination charge check
Bundle, landline, email and accessibility checks
ux_ui_requirements: Use the existing Key Takeaways panel to answer the task before the long guide, serving readers who need the rule and next action quickly.
Add a compact process table that separates the customer's action, new provider's action and old provider's action, serving readers confused about who cancels.
Use numbered step headings and checklists for contract, deal and switch-day tasks, reflecting the dominant task pattern across all three ranking pages.
Place visible regulator and primary-source citations directly beside material rights, timing and compensation claims.
Keep the existing accessible comparison deal table and FAQ accordion, with the comparison call to action after the checklist.
functional_requirements: Retain the existing live DealTable and /compare route so users can move from guidance to address-specific offers.
Retain FAQPage structured data and ensure every displayed answer is 35 to 90 words and matches the JSON-LD.
Provide direct links to Ofcom switching, contract-status and compensation pages for verification and problem resolution.
research_summary: Current UK results lead with One Touch Switch, checking contract status and a short numbered process. Which? is the focused version, MSE expands into savings and provider incentives, and Citizens Advice expands into rights and bundled services. The rebuilt guide adopts the useful summary, checklist, process table, problem route and comparison action while giving Ofcom claims stronger close citation.
depth_rationale: A 1,500-word rendered minimum is above the focused Which? result and substantial enough to cover Citizens Advice-style safeguards, while remaining well below MSE's broad hub because social tariffs, speed selection and provider-by-provider cancellation rules already have dedicated BroadbandPicker pages. This depth directly answers the switching task without padding adjacent topics.
